newsitem.title: THAILAND: Sluggish economy puts brakes on Thai car market.
newsitem.headline: Sluggish economy puts brakes on Thai car market.

text.p: The slowing economy is putting the brakes on growth in Thailand's once booming car market, analysts said on Monday.

"Car sales are expected to grow only slightly this year because slower economic growth will certainly reduce demand for new cars," Surapong Phasitpatnapong, spokesman for the Thai Automotive Industry Association (TAIA), told Reuters.
Statistics from Toyota Motor (Thailand) Corp show that total car sales in Thailand rose 3.1 percent in 1996 to 589,126 units from 571,580 the previous year.
The association expected total 1997 car sales of around 600,000, Surapong said.
Thailand's economic growth was about 6.7 last year, the slowest pace in a decade. The central bank predicts gross domestic product growth of 7.1 this year.
Analysts said the only chance of more than 600,000 cars being sold this year was if government measures to help shore up the economy and exports proved effective.

"The target of 600,000 units this year is a conservative figure. If the economy picks up, the number will be higher," said Ninnart Chaithirapinyo, senior managing director at Toyota Motor (Thailand), a unit of Toyota Motor Corp.
Ninnart said another factor that could help boost the car industry was central bank easing of controls on loans for car purchases.
The central bank late last year announced that it would not limit loans granted by commercial banks in 1997 as the sagging economy had caused a sharp slowing in credit growth.
The car market would also see stiffer competition as car makers tried to offload inventories once production expands, analysts said.
"The market this year will still be the market of the buyers. The intense competition will provide customers with new models and low prices," Ninnart said.
But exports of Thai-made vehicles and parts were expected to rise over the next few years with the move by several major car makers into Thailand, Ninnart said.
The value of Thai exports of assembled vehicles and parts rose 10.4 percent in the first 11 months of 1996 to 10.79 billion baht ($431.6 million) from 9.77 billion in the year-earlier period.
General Motors Corp last year said it would build a $750 million plant in Thailand and that more than half of the Opel sedans built at the plant would be exported to other countries in the region.
Ford Motor Co has also teamed up with Mazda Motor Corp to produce light pick-up trucks in Thailand for export.
Honda Motor Corp last October made Thailand its Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) headquarters.
